data.body:
## RCA — Phase 1 complete (rebar-debug)

**Classification: `defect`** (an **omission**, not a regression — the returncode check was never
written at either site; there is no good→bad transition to bisect).

### Proven mechanism

Both named sites derive their *entire* verdict from the absence of a string in a real child's
captured output, and never consult `returncode`. A child killed by a signal is torn down by the
kernel before it writes, so `stdout == stderr == ""`, the substring is trivially absent, and the
oracle reports GREEN for a run that never executed.

The changeable artifacts:

- `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py:127` —
  `assert "::error::" not in (result.stdout + result.stderr)`, the whole body of
  `test_absent_floor_file_emits_no_workflow_error`. `_run_gate` (same file, ~line 54) is a bare
  `subprocess.run([...], capture_output=True)` — no `check=True`, no returncode assertion.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:151` —
  `assert "unknown subcommand 'reconcile'" not in (cp.stdout + cp.stderr).lower()`, the sole
  assertion of `test_reconcile_intercepted_dry_run_default`. `_cli` (line 22) likewise never
  checks the returncode.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:228` and `:242` — `returncode != 0`,
  which a `-9` satisfies, so the returncode check is present but the wrong shape.

### Proof (discriminating experiments, both run)

**Experiment A — the oracle expressions, against a real killed child.** A child running
`os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGKILL)` was spawned for real (not a hand-built
`CompletedProcess`). Observed: `returncode=-9  stdout=''  stderr=''`. Feeding that into each of
the three assertion expressions verbatim:

```
SITE 1 ORACLE: PASSES (GREEN) on a signal-killed child  <-- FAIL-OPEN
SITE 2 ORACLE: PASSES (GREEN) on a signal-killed child  <-- FAIL-OPEN
SITE 3 ORACLE (returncode != 0): PASSES on a signal-killed child <-- does not close the gap
```

**Experiment B — the real test bodies, driven under pytest.** `subprocess.run` was monkeypatched
inside each test module to spawn the suicide child instead of the intended one, and the *actual*
test functions were invoked. pytest reported **2 passed**:

```
SITE1: real test body PASSED against a child that never ran
SITE2: real test body PASSED against a child that never ran
```

Experiment B is the discriminating one: A alone could be dismissed as a statement about a
substring, B shows the shipped test functions themselves report green when the thing they guard
never ran. It also rules out the rival explanation that some fixture, `conftest`, or helper
already asserts the child's exit — nothing intercepted the killed child anywhere in either call
chain.

### Authoritative source the behaviour violates

- Closed bug `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508` and closed bug `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` (`plan_defect`) — the
  same construct class was adjudicated a defect twice and fixed in `tests/e2e` and the live-DC
  tier respectively.
- The design invariant is written down in-repo: `tests/_child_diag.py:56-79`,
  `assert_child_ran_clean`'s docstring — *"WHY the returncode is checked AT ALL, and why FIRST …
  That is a fail-OPEN … the returncode is therefore checked BEFORE the traceback."*

### Attribution — omission, by scope-of-work (three origins, one per site)

There is no introducing commit that *broke* working behaviour; line-scoped `git blame -w -C -M`
on the assertion lines lands on the commits that first authored them, each of which shipped the
oracle already fail-open. Attribution is therefore by scope-of-work, per the omission case.

| Site | blame (line-scoped) | date | origin ticket |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — `test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py:127` | `c4c4e1782db` | 2026-08-04 | **`7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14`** (`rebar-ticket:` trailer) |
| 2 — `test_cli.py:151` | `04117bd74a8` | 2026-06-08 | **no ticket** — pre-trailer-convention commit |
| 3 — `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:228,242` | `8593a7e7cb9` | 2026-08-12 | **`8aed-e264-7112-4c2f`** (`rebar-ticket:` trailer) |

`caused_by` is recorded against `7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14` — site 1 is the primary site (a
*success/health* oracle, the dangerous direction) and its commit authored the whole test
including its sole assertion, so a reviewer of that change could plausibly have caught it.
`8aed-e264-7112-4c2f` is recorded as a second `caused_by` for site 3.

**Site 2 is unattributable to a ticket, and here is the search.** `git log -S"unknown subcommand
'reconcile'"` over `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` (and its pre-move path
`tests/interfaces/test_cli.py`) returns exactly one commit, `04117bd74a8` (2026-06-08); it
carries neither a `rebar-ticket:` trailer nor a leading `<id>:` subject, predating that
convention. The later commit that rewrote the surrounding test body — `914891b016a`
(2026-06-11, ticket `e4c3-757a-161b-48c3`) — is deliberately **not** named: blame shows it did
not touch line 151, and naming it would be blaming the most recent toucher rather than the
origin.

**Divergence from the blame default, stated explicitly.** A whole-file blame majority on either
file would name a much more recent toucher (the files have been edited many times since). The
line-scoped blame above is what produced these three, and it disagrees with that default.

**Why the origins are NOT `f0fb` / `0e1d`.** The tempting "unmet obligation" reading — those
tickets created the *"a child-output oracle must check the returncode first"* contract and these
sites were never updated to it — was considered and rejected on dates. `tests/_child_diag.py`
was created 2026-08-20, *after* all three sites existed, so no site could have been updated to a
contract that did not yet exist. And `0e1d` did not ship past its consumers: its Step-7 sweep is
what filed **this** ticket (`discovered_from 0e1d`). That is the opposite of a defect escape,
and charging it would corrupt the metric it feeds.

### Caller-dependency gate

Cleared in one look — the change is confined to three test functions. Nothing imports or calls
them; the only shared artifact touched is `tests/_child_diag.py`, which is imported (read-only,
no signature change planned) by `tests/e2e/conftest.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_dc_pass_health.py`,
and the live-DC tier.

### Scope note

Restoration only. The fix makes each oracle *honest about when it cannot conclude* — asserting
the child ran to completion before trusting an absence derived from its output. It does not
widen what any oracle asserts about the product.
